question:
(i) What type of spectrum is produced by an excited rarefied atomic gas?
(ii) Why does this spectrum contain only certain wavelengths?

options.A:
(i) A continuous spectrum is produced.
(ii) The gas emits every possible wavelength.
options.B:
(i) An absorption line spectrum is produced.
(ii) The gas absorbs all wavelengths from its surroundings.
options.C:
(i) An excited rarefied atomic gas produces an emission line spectrum, consisting of bright lines on a dark background.
(ii) Its atoms emit only at certain definite frequencies or wavelengths, so the spectrum is not continuous.
options.D:
(i) A continuous spectrum with no lines is produced.
(ii) Excited atoms cannot emit radiation.
